# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, which states that the light cycles through three colours each round, and the green wire must be cut when the light is green.

However, I cannot speak, nor can I touch the bomb. I can only gesture to Deaf. Deaf sees the bomb (the light's current colour and the wires' colours/positions), Blind can touch the bomb, and Deaf can speak aloud to both Blind and me.

As noted in the rules, a sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something. Sending undefined gestures right now would only cause confusion, and I do not yet know the layout of the bomb or what Deaf sees. I will wait for Deaf to inspect the bomb, speak to us, and establish a protocol or describe what is present.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have 3 wires, positions 1, 2, 3. My only available action is act(op="cut", position=N). Coordinate with Deaf via gestures; Deaf can speak aloud to tell me which wire to cut.
Deaf says: Bomb state: Display is 0. Light is yellow. Wires: 1 is green, 2 is yellow, 3 is blue. Mute, Blind cannot see gestures, so gesture instructions to me and I will speak them aloud to Blind.

I have reviewed the defusal manual and the current bomb state reported by Deaf and Blind.

The defusal manual specifies that the light cycles through three colours each round, and the green wire (wire 1) must be cut specifically when the light is green. Currently, the light is yellow (round 1) and will cycle. Because Blind moves before Deaf in each round, Blind must not cut blindly; Blind must wait until the round in which the light is green.

To communicate to Deaf that we must wait and that the rule is green light to green wire (1 -> 1):
- `✋`: Wait / hold / stop.
- `☝ 👉 ☝`: 1 -> 1 (when light is colour 1 / green, cut wire 1 / green).

This signals to Deaf to hold off on cutting immediately and conveys the condition (1 -> 1), allowing Deaf to confirm with us or time Blind's action for the green light round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "☝", "👉", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: Light has changed from yellow to ORANGE. Display is 0. Wires: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Blind: Mute gestured [✋, ☝, 👉, ☝] — open hand/palm/press, pointing up (1), pointing right, pointing up (1). If you have directional buttons/D-pad, this looks like UP, RIGHT, UP (or Press/Enter then UP, RIGHT, UP). Blind, please speak aloud what controls/parts you feel. Mute: gesture 👍 if UP, RIGHT, UP is correct, or 👎 if not.

Deaf asked whether the sequence represents directional inputs (UP, RIGHT, UP) for a D-pad or buttons. Because Blind only possesses wires 1, 2, and 3 with the cut operation, and the defusal rule depends strictly on cutting wire 1 (green) when the cycling light is green, the directional interpretation is completely incorrect.

Following the principle that a sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something, Deaf explicitly established that 👍 means correct and 👎 means incorrect. I will respond with 👎 to dismiss the directional hypothesis so Deaf and Blind can refocus on the wires and establish a precise yes/no or counting protocol.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Deaf cannot hear speech, but you can hear me. I have NO buttons or D-pad at all. My ONLY possible action is act(op="cut", position=N) where N is 1, 2, or 3. The bomb has 3 wires: 1 is green, 2 is yellow, 3 is blue. Display is 0. Light is orange. Please check the wire-cutting rules in the manual, then gesture to Deaf (e.g. 1 finger for wire 1, 2 for wire 2, 3 for wire 3) and have Deaf speak to me which wire to cut.
Deaf says: Update: Light is now GREEN. Display is 0. Wires: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Blind: Please speak aloud what components you can interact with (buttons, dial, wires to cut, display buttons). Mute hears you! Mute: since you hear me, let's use this simple gesture code: ✊ = CUT wire, ✋ = PRESS button/hold. ☝ = 1, ✌ = 2, 🤟 = 3. For display: 👆 = up, 👇 = down. Please send the action and the number.

I have reviewed the manual and the bomb cycle. The manual mandates cutting the green wire (wire 1) only when the cycling light is green.

The light cycles across rounds in the sequence:
- Round 1: Yellow
- Round 2: Orange
- Round 3: Green
- Round 4: Yellow
- Round 5: Orange
- Round 6: Green

The turn order each round is strictly Mute -> Blind -> Deaf. 
If I signal the cut command to Deaf in Round 5, Deaf will receive it at the end of Round 5 and speak to Blind. Blind will then receive Deaf's instruction at the start of Round 6 and cut wire 1 during Round 6, precisely when the light is green.

Sending the cut command now in Round 4 would cause Blind to cut during Round 5 when the light is orange, triggering detonation. Therefore, I will wait in Round 4 and signal the cut in Round 5.

```
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: REMINDER: I am DEAF and cannot hear any speech. If Blind spoke aloud, only Mute heard it! Mute, you must relay instructions to me via gestures so I can speak them to Blind. Current bomb state: Display is 0. Light is cycling (YELLOW -> ORANGE -> GREEN). Wires: 1 is green, 2 is yellow, 3 is blue. Mute, please gesture the instruction now: ✊ + [☝/✌/🤟] to CUT wire 1, 2, or 3. ✋ to press button. 👆/👇 to change display. Blind, hold on until Mute gestures instructions.

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute instructs you to CUT WIRE 1! (Wire 1 is green / the first wire). Current light is orange, display is 0.

I have verified that the timing matches the defusal manual: Deaf observed an orange light in Round 5, so the light cycles to green in Round 6. Blind has received Deaf's instruction to cut wire 1 and will execute the cut in Round 6 when the light is green. I will wait.

```
wait()
```
